subject: accounting
title: ZIMSEC O-Level Principles of Accounting

officialDocument.title: Principles of Accounting Syllabus, Forms 1 - 4, 2015 - 2022 (Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, Curriculum Development and Technical Services), examined by ZIMSEC at O Level
officialDocument.publisher: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (Curriculum Development and Technical Services) / Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC)

sourceNote: Topic names and their order are transcribed from the topic list (6.0) of the Ministry's Principles of Accounting Syllabus Forms 1 - 4 (2015 - 2022); the content of each topic and the form in which it is taught come from the scope and sequence (7.0) and the competency matrix (8.0). The document does not number its topics: every topic, sub-topic and objective code here is ours. Learning-objective statements are our own paraphrase; no syllabus text is reproduced.
notes: Source (read 2026-10-08): the Mashonaland West provincial education office's copy of the Ministry document, file 'Form 1-4 Accounting Syllabus.pdf' (http://www.mopsemashwest.gov.zw/files/Form%201-4%20Accounting%20Syllabus.pdf; the site's https certificate has expired, so the https URL recorded here may not load), read through a text rendering. The cover prints 'Forms 1 - 4' and '2015 - 2022' and the copyright year 2015. The scope-and-sequence and competency-matrix tables come out of the text rendering with their columns scrambled; the form assigned to each item is read from the column positions and cross-checked against the matrix, and some items (accounting concepts, closing entries, provisions, depreciation by revaluation, correction of errors) appear only in the scope and sequence. Check every heading, the form of each item and each objective against a clean copy from ZIMSEC.
Subject code: not printed in the syllabus document. ZIMSEC O-Level Principles of Accounting is commonly cited as 7112; confirm it (code left null).

Version dates: assumed first examined in November 2018 (effectiveFrom 2018-01-01), as for the other 2015-2022 files. Under the Heritage-Based Curriculum (2024-2030) new syllabi were issued; confirm which syllabus the November 2026 and later O-Level Principles of Accounting examinations use, set effectiveTo, and create a new version file when a new syllabus replaces this one.

Assessment (9.0) as read: continuous assessment 30% (theory tests, practical assignments and projects in Forms 1 to 4: Form 1 5%, Form 2 5%, Form 3 10%, Form 4 10%) and a summative examination 70%: Paper 1, 40 multiple-choice questions with four options, all compulsory (40 marks, 20% of the subject); Paper 2, five compulsory structured questions of 20 marks each (100 marks, 50% of the subject). The specification grid prints '1 1/2 hours' twice in a scrambled table; both papers are recorded as 1 hour 30 minutes, which must be confirmed (a 100-mark structured paper is often longer). Calculator rules are not stated.
Assessment objective 2 allows ledger accounts in 'T' account, running balance or balanced journal format; content may use either the T-account or the three-column running balance layout.

The document mixes older and newer terms (income statement, statement of financial position, trade receivables and payables, inventory, but also profit and loss account, provision for doubtful debts and stock in teaching practice); content uses the syllabus's terms and gives the Cambridge equivalents.

Not in this syllabus (taught in the family for Cambridge IGCSE only): valuation of inventory at the lower of cost and net realisable value, data storage and sustainability, inter-business comparison and the limitations of accounting statements, return on capital employed and the receivables, payables and inventory-days ratios. The project and practical assignments are continuous assessment only and are not simulated.
overview: The ZIMSEC O-Level Principles of Accounting syllabus (Forms 1-4) takes learners through the accounting cycle: source documents, subsidiary books, the ledger and trial balance, then end-of-year financial statements and adjustments for sole traders, followed by control accounts, bank reconciliation, ratios, incomplete records, non-trading concerns, departmental and manufacturing accounts, partnerships, company accounts and business ethics. It stresses practical skills for small to medium enterprises, enterprise and Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu (good business ethics).
assessmentOverview: Continuous assessment (theory tests, practical assignments and projects, Forms 1-4) carries 30%. The examination carries 70%: Paper 1 has 40 compulsory four-option multiple-choice questions (40 marks, 20%) and Paper 2 has five compulsory structured questions of 20 marks each (100 marks, 50%).

components.name: Paper 1: Multiple choice
components.description: 40 compulsory multiple-choice questions with four options each, covering the whole syllabus.

components.name: Paper 2: Structured questions
components.description: Five compulsory structured questions of 20 marks each.

topics.name: Introduction to Principles of Accounting
topics.description: Form 1: accounting terms, types of business activity and organisation, the importance of accounting and its users.

objectives.text: Form 1: define business, accounting, transaction, book-keeping, capital, assets, liabilities, income, expenses and profit.
Form 1: state, explain and distinguish trading, manufacturing and service activities and sole proprietors, partnerships and limited companies.
Form 1: explain why accounting is important and identify the users of accounting information.

topics.name: The Accounting Cycle
topics.description: Form 1: transactions, source documents, subsidiary books, ledger, trial balance and financial statements.

objectives.text: Form 1: define, illustrate and explain the stages of the accounting cycle in order.

topics.name: Data Processing Methods: Manual and Electronic
topics.description: Forms 1 and 3: manual and electronic methods of processing accounting data.

objectives.text: Form 1: name the methods of processing accounting data and list the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Form 3: apply manual methods and demonstrate the use of electronic methods of processing data.

topics.name: Source Documents
topics.description: Form 1: receipts, cheques, invoices, debit notes, credit notes, vouchers, bank statements and statements of account.

objectives.text: Form 1: describe each source document, explain its significance and match it to the subsidiary book in which it is recorded.

topics.name: Subsidiary Books
topics.description: Forms 1 to 3: the books of original entry.

children.name: Cash books
children.description: Form 1: the two-column cash book. Form 2: the three-column cash book, trade and cash discounts.

objectives.text: Form 1: record transactions in a two-column cash book and interpret its entries.
Form 2: define and calculate trade and cash discounts and record transactions in a three-column cash book.

children.name: Sales, purchases and returns journals
children.description: Form 1: sales journal, purchases journal, sales returns journal and purchases returns journal.

objectives.text: Form 1: label the columns of the subsidiary books, classify transactions and record them in the correct journal.
Form 1: explain and interpret the entries in the subsidiary books.

children.name: Petty cash book
children.description: Form 2: the purpose and use of the petty cash book.

objectives.text: Form 2: explain the purpose of the petty cash book and record transactions in it.

children.name: General journal
children.description: Forms 2 and 3: the general journal (journal proper).

objectives.text: Forms 2 and 3: state the uses of the general journal, prepare and post journal entries and interpret them.

topics.name: The Ledger
topics.description: Forms 1 to 3: classification, posting and balancing of ledger accounts, folio numbers and the types of ledger.

objectives.text: Form 1: classify transactions, post entries from the subsidiary books to the ledger and balance the accounts.
Forms 2 and 3: use folio numbers and post entries to the trade receivables ledger, trade payables ledger and general ledger.
Forms 1 to 3: explain the entries in ledger accounts and interpret their final balances.

topics.name: Trial Balance and Errors
topics.description: Forms 1 to 4: preparing a trial balance, errors, the suspense account and the effect of errors on profit.

objectives.text: Forms 1 and 2: define a trial balance, explain its purposes and construct one from ledger balances.

children.name: Errors not revealed by the trial balance
children.description: Form 2: errors that do not affect trial balance agreement.

objectives.text: Form 2: state and explain the errors that a trial balance does not reveal.

children.name: Correction of errors and the suspense account
children.description: Form 3: correction of errors, the suspense account and correcting the trial balance.

objectives.text: Form 3: correct errors by journal entries, open and clear a suspense account and correct the trial balance.

children.name: Effect of errors on profit
children.description: Form 4: adjustments to gross and net profit and revised statements after the correction of errors.

objectives.text: Form 4: explain the effect of errors on profit and adjust gross or net profit after correcting them.
Form 4: prepare revised statements of profit and of financial position (extracts) after the correction of errors.

topics.name: Accounting Concepts
topics.description: Form 3 (scope and sequence): matching/accrual, prudence, going concern, consistency, historical cost and double entry.

objectives.text: Form 3: explain the listed accounting concepts and apply them in preparing financial statements.

topics.name: End of Year Financial Statements
topics.description: Forms 2 and 3: the income statement and statement of financial position, closing entries and the interpretation of financial statements.

objectives.text: Form 2: define the income statement, explain why it is needed and draw one up for a sole trader.
Form 2: define the statement of financial position and prepare one for a sole trader.
Form 3: make the closing entries that transfer income and expenses to the income statement.
Form 3: interpret financial statements for the benefit of their users.

topics.name: End of Year Adjustments
topics.description: Forms 2 and 3: accruals and prepayments, depreciation and disposals, provisions, and financial statements with adjustments.

children.name: Accruals and prepayments
children.description: Form 2: for income and expenses in the financial statements only (ledger accounts not required). Form 3: ledger accounts of income and expenses.

objectives.text: Form 2: define accruals and prepayments and show the adjustments in end-of-year financial statements.
Form 3: prepare ledger accounts for income and expenses with accruals and prepayments.

children.name: Depreciation and disposal of non-current assets
children.description: Form 2: causes of depreciation, straight-line and reducing-balance methods. Form 3: accounting for depreciation (including the revaluation method) and disposals.

objectives.text: Form 2: define depreciation, state its causes and calculate it by the straight-line and reducing-balance methods.
Form 3: account for depreciation by the straight-line, reducing-balance and revaluation methods.
Form 3: record the disposal of non-current assets.

children.name: Provisions for doubtful debts and discounts allowable
children.description: Form 3 (scope and sequence). Writing off bad (irrecoverable) debts is not listed separately but underlies the provision for doubtful debts.

objectives.text: Form 3: create and adjust provisions for doubtful debts and for discounts allowable and record them.

children.name: Income statement and statement of financial position with adjustments

objectives.text: Form 3: prepare the income statement and statement of financial position after year-end adjustments.

topics.name: Capital and Revenue Expenditure
topics.description: Form 2: definitions and differences. Form 3: accounting treatment and the effects of incorrect classification.

objectives.text: Form 2: define and distinguish capital and revenue expenditure.
Form 3: show capital and revenue expenditure correctly in the financial statements.
Form 3: state the effects of incorrect classification on profit, non-current assets and working capital.

topics.name: Control Accounts
topics.description: Form 3: purposes, types, sources of information and preparation.

objectives.text: Form 3: define control accounts, state their purposes, name their types and identify their sources of information.
Form 3: prepare sales ledger and purchases ledger control accounts.

topics.name: Bank Reconciliation
topics.description: Form 2: bank reconciliation statements. Form 3: errors, the updated cash book and bank overdrafts.

objectives.text: Form 2: define bank reconciliation statements, explain their importance, state the causes of differences and prepare them.
Form 3: identify errors in the cash book and bank statement and draw up an updated cash book.
Form 3: prepare bank reconciliation statements, including the treatment of a bank overdraft.

topics.name: Accounting Ratios
topics.description: Form 4: profitability ratios (mark-up, margin, net profit percentage) and liquidity ratios (current ratio, quick ratio, rate of inventory turnover).

objectives.text: Form 4: recall the profitability and liquidity ratio formulae and compute the ratios.
Form 4: apply the ratios to arrive at missing figures.

topics.name: Single Entry and Incomplete Records
topics.description: Form 4: statements of affairs, missing figures and financial statements.

objectives.text: Form 4: define the terms and calculate opening and closing capital using statements of affairs.
Form 4: calculate missing sales, purchases, expenses, gross profit, net profit, drawings and income.
Form 4: draw up end-of-year financial statements from incomplete records.

topics.name: Not for Profit Making Organisations (Non-Trading Concerns)
topics.description: Form 2: key terms, receipts and payments accounts, income and expenditure accounts and statements of financial position. Form 4: sources of income, subscriptions accounts, missing figures and trading accounts of profit-making projects.

objectives.text: Form 2: define surplus, deficit, accumulated fund and subscriptions, and draw up receipts and payments accounts.
Form 2: prepare simple income and expenditure accounts and statements of financial position.
Form 4: state sources of income, construct subscriptions accounts with adjustments and deduce missing figures.
Form 4: compile trading accounts for profit-making projects and prepare income and expenditure accounts and statements of financial position.

topics.name: Departmental Accounts
topics.description: Form 3: departmental trading accounts, apportionment of expenses and the combined profit and loss account.

objectives.text: Form 3: state the purpose of departmental trading accounts and prepare them in columnar form.
Form 3: apportion expenses among departments and draw up a combined profit and loss account and statement of financial position.

topics.name: Manufacturing Accounts
topics.description: Form 4: direct and indirect costs, prime cost, work in progress, income statements and statements of financial position.

objectives.text: Form 4: define and classify manufacturing costs.
Form 4: prepare manufacturing accounts, income statements and statements of financial position.

topics.name: Partnership Formation: End of Year Financial Statements
topics.description: Form 4: formation, advantages and disadvantages, income statements, appropriation accounts, capital and current accounts and statements of financial position.

objectives.text: Form 4: define a partnership, state reasons for forming one and outline the importance and contents of a partnership agreement.
Form 4: prepare appropriation accounts.
Form 4: prepare current and capital accounts and statements of financial position showing current accounts within or outside the statement.

topics.name: Company Accounts
topics.description: Form 4: terms (shares, debentures, share capital, shareholders' funds, dividends, reserves, retained profits), statements of changes in equity and statements of financial position (extracts).

objectives.text: Form 4: define company accounting terms, outline the capital structure of a company and state the advantages of forming a company.
Form 4: prepare statements of changes in equity and statements of financial position (capital structure extracts).

topics.name: Business Ethics
topics.description: Form 4: professionalism, integrity, confidentiality, competence, objectivity and compliance.

objectives.text: Form 4: define business ethics and identify the professional ethics in accounting.
Form 4: apply business ethics in day-to-day business transactions.
